items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The lighthouse keeper had logged the weather every day for thirty years. On the morning he retired, he left the logbook open on the desk with a single new line: 'Clear skies. Someone else's turn to watch.' He did not look back as he walked down the hill.

Claim A: The keeper felt at peace handing over his duty. Claim B: The keeper regretted his decision to retire. Which claim is better supported by evidence, and why is the other weak?
items.answer: Claim A is better supported. The calm final entry ('Someone else's turn to watch') and his not looking back suggest acceptance and peace. Claim B is weak because nothing in the text shows regret; his steady, forward-facing exit points away from it.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Every report card, Devon's grades were average, but his teacher wrote the same comment each time: 'Asks the questions no one else dares to ask.' Devon kept the comments in a drawer and reread them whenever he felt ordinary.

Claim A: Devon valued being curious more than getting top grades. Claim B: Devon was a poor student. Which claim does the evidence support, and why is the other unfair?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; Devon saved and reread the comments praising his questions, showing he valued curiosity. Claim B is unfair and unsupported, because 'average' grades plus praised curiosity do not make him a poor student, and the text never calls him one.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The painting hung in the hallway for years before anyone learned that the quiet janitor had made it. When the principal offered to display it in the lobby with his name, he shook his head. 'I painted it for the building,' he said, 'not for the credit.'

Claim A: The janitor cared more about the work than about recognition. Claim B: The janitor was ashamed of his painting. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he declined the credit and said he painted 'for the building, not for the credit,' valuing the work itself. Claim B is contradicted, because refusing credit out of humility is different from shame, and nothing suggests he was ashamed.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Wei practiced the piano piece until midnight, then erased his name from the recital sign-up sheet and wrote in his nervous friend's instead. 'You've earned it more than me,' he told her the next day.

Claim A: Wei believed his friend deserved the chance. Claim B: Wei could not play the piece well. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted by the text?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; Wei said his friend had earned it more and gave her his spot. Claim B is contradicted, since he practiced the piece until midnight, showing he could play it; he stepped aside by choice.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The village had not seen rain in weeks. When the first drops fell, the children ran outside laughing, but old Ananya stayed on her porch, eyes closed, whispering a thank-you to the sky.

Claim A: Ananya felt deep gratitude for the rain. Claim B: Ananya disliked the children's noise. Which claim does the evidence best support, and why is the other unsupported?
items.answer: Claim A is best supported; with eyes closed she whispered a thank-you to the sky, showing deep gratitude. Claim B is unsupported, since the text never connects her stillness to dislike of the children; she is simply absorbed in her own thankfulness.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Carlos turned down the captain's armband, asking the coach to give it to the teammate who had been at every practice. 'I miss too many for work,' he admitted, 'and a captain should be there for the team.'

Claim A: Carlos thought reliability mattered in a leader. Claim B: Carlos did not care about the team. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; Carlos said a captain 'should be there for the team' and chose the more reliable teammate. Claim B is contradicted, because caring about who leads well is itself a sign that he cares about the team.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The bookstore was closing for good. On the last day, the owner gave away the unsold books for free, but she kept one worn copy of poems for herself and pressed it to her chest before locking the door.

Claim A: The poetry book held personal meaning for the owner. Claim B: The owner did not value books. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; she kept the worn poetry book and pressed it to her chest, showing personal meaning. Claim B is contradicted, since giving books away gently and treasuring one shows she valued books deeply.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Yara stayed silent when the teacher praised the group's project, even though she had done most of the late-night work. Later she told only her journal, 'It felt good to see them happy.'

Claim A: Yara found quiet satisfaction in her teammates' joy. Claim B: Yara resented her teammates. Which claim does the evidence support, and why is the other weak?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; her journal line, 'It felt good to see them happy,' shows quiet satisfaction. Claim B is weak because she expresses gladness, not resentment, even though she could have spoken up for credit.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The retired teacher returned every September to watch the new students arrive, sitting on the same bench across the street. She never went inside. 'It is their school now,' she said when asked.

Claim A: The teacher had made peace with no longer working there. Claim B: The teacher was bitter about retiring. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; she returns fondly and says 'It is their school now,' showing acceptance. Claim B is contradicted, because bitterness would not fit her gentle yearly visits or her generous comment.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Idris gave his umbrella to a stranger at the bus stop and walked the last mile home in the rain. When his mother asked why he was soaked, he only shrugged and said the other man had farther to go.

Claim A: Idris put a stranger's comfort ahead of his own. Claim B: Idris forgot his umbrella that day. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he gave away his umbrella because the man 'had farther to go,' putting the stranger first. Claim B is contradicted, since he clearly had the umbrella and chose to give it away.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The chess club's best player, Nour, deliberately taught her opponents the strategies that had beaten them, even though it meant tougher games for her later.

Claim A: Nour valued helping others improve over staying unbeatable. Claim B: Nour was afraid of losing. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; she taught rivals the strategies despite tougher future games, valuing their growth. Claim B is contradicted, because someone afraid of losing would not hand opponents the tools to beat her.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

After winning the essay prize, Talia learned that a classmate had narrowly missed it. She copied her own notes and offered to help him prepare for next year's contest.

Claim A: Talia wanted her classmate to succeed too. Claim B: Talia felt guilty for winning. Which claim is better supported, and why is the other uncertain?
items.answer: Claim A is better supported; sharing her notes and offering to help shows she wanted his success. Claim B is uncertain, because the text shows generosity without stating guilt as the reason.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The farmer left one corner of every field unharvested. When a traveler asked why he wasted good grain, he said, 'It is not waste. It is for whoever passes by hungry.'

Claim A: The farmer left grain on purpose to help others. Claim B: The farmer was careless with his crops. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he said the grain was 'for whoever passes by hungry,' a deliberate act of giving. Claim B is contradicted, since the choice was intentional generosity, not carelessness.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Min-jun practiced his speech in the empty auditorium each night. On the day of the contest, he gave his prepared time slot to a trembling younger student and said he would be happy to go last, or not at all.

Claim A: Min-jun was willing to set aside his own moment for someone more nervous. Claim B: Min-jun was unprepared for the contest. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he gave his slot to the trembling student and offered to go last or not at all. Claim B is contradicted, since he had practiced every night, showing he was well prepared.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The orchard owner hired the same workers every year, even the slowest one, an old man who could barely fill a basket. 'He taught me this trade,' she explained, 'and a debt like that does not expire.'

Claim A: The owner kept the old man out of loyalty and gratitude. Claim B: The old man was the orchard's most productive worker. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; she kept him because 'a debt like that does not expire,' showing loyalty and gratitude. Claim B is contradicted, since the text says he could 'barely fill a basket.'
